text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[128,256],"block_K":[64,128],"num_stages":[2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.2,"launches":1.2,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":0.6},"rationale":"Four attempts observed. Best is attempt-03 at 156.26 us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM), slightly beating attempt-00 (157.29 us; block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0, 2 blocks/SM). attempts-01/02 (block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256, swizzle 16 vs 64) both simulated 186.64 us with identical traffic/blocks-per-SM, so swizzle panel size produced no measurable latency change on this geometry and small-tile/short-block_K regime is rejected. All attempts compiled and passed numerics/SMT. Revision: drop block_M=16/32 and block_K=32/128-for-small-tiles; keep block_M=64/128, block_K=64/128, block_N=128/256 to test untested wider-N/fewer-launch and block_K=128 deeper-work hypotheses. Stages 2-4 (stage=1 was fast at attempt-00 but only with 256 threads; keep 2-4 to explore overlap). Threads 128/256 retained since 128 won attempt-03 and 256 won attempt-00 - feedback must disambiguate; swizzle trimmed to [0,4,8] since 16/64 were equivalent and M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows. Weights: footprint lowered to 0.6 (smem at cap but not the binding limiter), pipeline raised to 1.5 to favor deeper K-overlap, traffic/launches each 1.2 as DRAM 34.6MB and block count dominate. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds, actual smem 32768). Next hypothesis: block_M=64 with block_N=128/256, block_K=64/128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256, swizzle=0/4 to test whether wider N reduces launches enough to beat 156.26 us. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
